programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.desc: Documentary filmmakers go to the most remote corners of our planet to discover the secrets of the few untouched ecosystems.From the Namib Desert to Patagonia, only a few places on Earth have remained largely unchanged.Isolated from the rest of the world, they managed to defend themselves against the most harmful effects of human interference.Life there goes on as nature intended.The creators will take viewers on an exciting journey to the last places that are paradise on earth.Amazing, breathtaking landscapes will be presented, as well as exciting behaviors of the most popular animals in the world.Each episode will feature a different unique corner of the globe - from the mysterious, fog-shrouded forests of Borneo to the lush beauty of Africa's Luangwa floodplain The tropical island of Borneo is located in the heart of Southeast Asia.Its area is as large as the US state of Texas, and its forests have remained unchanged for 140 million years.Areas bathed in sunlight are cooled by heavy rainfall.Such greenhouse conditions resulted in the development of approximately 60,000 species of plants and animals there over time.In terms of biology, this island is one of the most diverse.Over 6,000 endemic species have evolved here in isolated conditions.The extraordinary wealth of nature arises from shallow, nutrient-poor soil.However, life managed to triumph here, transforming this place into a unique paradise on earth.

programme.title: Frozen Planet 2
programme.desc: Eleven years after the premiere of "The Frozen Planet", viewers will take part in the second stage of the journey through the icy lands of Earth.Narrator Sir David Attenborough will take them to both poles and take a closer look at animals that also live outside the polar region, in the coldest regions of the world: among mountain peaks, in frozen deserts, in snow-covered forests and ice-covered oceans.The diversity of the ecosystems of these lands is surprising, and the fact that they seem untouched by humans adds to their magic.The conditions here are extremely harsh, so only animal heroes live there.On vast snow plains, wolves hunt huge bison, whales use clever techniques to capture their prey, and rare Siberian tigers glide silently across the white powder.However, as a result of the unprecedented rate of temperature increase, these icy lands are disappearing before our eyes.Scientists discuss the true impact of these changes not only on the life of fauna, flora and people, but also on the entire planet.

programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.desc: Documentary filmmakers go to the most remote corners of our planet to discover the secrets of the few untouched ecosystems.From the Namib Desert to Patagonia, only a few places on Earth have remained largely unchanged.Isolated from the rest of the world, they managed to defend themselves against the most harmful effects of human interference.Life there goes on as nature intended.The creators will take viewers on an exciting journey to the last places that are paradise on earth.Amazing, breathtaking landscapes will be presented, as well as exciting behaviors of the most popular animals in the world.Each episode will feature a different unique corner of the globe - from the mysterious, fog-shrouded forests of Borneo to the lush beauty of Africa's Luangwa floodplain A story about the Namib Desert and the Skeleton Coast.The drought there seems not to be conducive to paradise living conditions.At noon the temperature exceeds 43 degrees Celsius.However, it turns out that this is the only desert inhabited by lions.There are also about 100,000 southern oryxes living here, and nature provides excellent conditions for one of the bird giants.There are numerous ostriches there.The rainfall that appears gives rise to a magical transformation.Seeds that have spent up to 15 years dormant transform the sand into a flowery meadow.The region is also inhabited by about 150 elephants.The Namib is the only desert where, against all odds, they managed to survive thanks to life-sustaining underground waters.

programme.title: The Search for the Last Unicorn
programme.desc: Reports from African residents about a northern rhinoceros sighted in South Sudan have given ecologists new hope that the animal, considered extinct in 2018, has been given a second chance.The BBC team accompanies an international team of naturalists who set off to a war-torn country that is one of the most dangerous places on Earth in search of traces of a white rhinoceros living in uninhabited areas of Africa.Scientists, includingAldo Kane and Paul Naden wonder whether it is possible for an animal about which we still know so little to survive.During the expedition, they use the latest technologies such as drones and try to do everything they can to find the rhinoceros, whose population has declined due to the illegal trade in its horns, which many people believe have healing properties.Filmmakers will also show such African animals as baboons, giraffes, antelopes, elephants and badgers.
